messages:
incident-bot: Pager — CRITICAL: Pegasus (pegasus-prod) VPC private deployment reports degraded egress to customer-managed NLB. Error rate spike, 503s, 60% of requests failing. Paging on-call.
alex_h: Acked. jumping in. any customer-facing impact?
maria_sre: Pegasus reports app timeouts to their internal services via their NLB target group. symptoms started ~6m ago. CI alert: upstream healthcheck failures (502/504) and connection reset.
priya_net: quick network check: NLB health checks are failing from our side. TCP handshake times out to the NLB IPs. Could be SG or route table change on the customer side, but correlation with our recent SG cleanup job on pegasus-vpc.
devon_oncall: @priya_net did the cleanup touch egress SGs for the private deployment? I ran the job a few hours ago for stale rules — paused it after noticing a warning for pegasus-prod but proceeded.
priya_net: digging. running describe on the VPC components. from console: `aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-0pegasus` shows egress rules empty (only default deny). That would block outbound health checks and node->NLB communication.
alex_h: if SG egress is empty that explains it. we need a rollback to previous SG policy ASAP.
maria_sre: Customer impact: pegged to Pegasus's Tenant API. User-facing requests that touch private VPC resources are timing out. CS notified. ETA for rollback?
priya_net: rolling back sg-0pegasus to snapshot from 1968764000. command: ```
# rollback
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0pegasus --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0pegasus --protocol tcp --port 80 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0
```
priya_net: executed. please verify healthchecks.
maria_sre: doing quick curl / health probes against NLB IPs from internal workers. `curl -v --connect-timeout 3 https://10.12.34.56/health` returned TLS handshake now, 200 OK. healthcheck back to green for 2/3 targets.
devon_oncall: good. can we confirm full traffic recovery for tenant pegasus-prod? eng-console-bot, any routing fallbacks hit?
eng-console-bot: Routing policy events: 1968765422 — automatic fallback attempted to dedicated-us-east-1 pool for tenant pegasus-prod due to degradation. 1968765436 — fallback rolled back after routing test passed. No throttles.
alex_h: ok rollback worked and traffic resumed. how did the SG cleanup job decide to remove egress? need postmortem root cause.
priya_net: preliminary: a filter matched 'unused egress rules' and incorrectly matched the pegasus SG because the tag convention changed (team:pegasus-prod -> team:pegasus). job used tag equality instead of prefix, so it removed needed rules. I've stopped the cleanup job and added a dry-run guard.
cs_taylor: I've told the customer (Pegasus SRE) we applied a temporary fix and are running verification for 30m before we call it resolved. they're on the call and appreciate the rapid rollback. asking about permanent remediation.
maria_sre: remediation plan: 1) revert SG cleanup filter logic and add committed rules whitelist for Private deployments; 2) add an extra safety check: if a SG is attached to instances in a tenant VPC with active Dedicated routing, do not auto-modify; 3) add an automated canary that hits NLB healthchecks pre-change.
alex_h: also add runbook step: if healthchecks fail and SG egress is empty, do immediate `authorize-security-group-egress` with port 443/80 to restore connectivity and page network team.
devon_oncall: telemetry shows error rate dropped to baseline ~5m after rollback. still seeing some slow tail latencies for a small subset of requests — likely transient connection churn.
priya_net: verified network path: `traceroute` from node -> NLB shows expected hops. no route table changes. only SG change.
cs_taylor: customer requested we extend monitoring window to 2 hours and a postmortem. assigned to @maria_sre + @priya_net.
alex_h: assigning incident owner: maria_sre. rough severity classification: Sev2 (customer impact with mitigation).
maria_sre: taking ownership. timeline + notes will be added to the postmortem doc. immediate next steps: 1) update cleanup job filters + add whitelist; 2) add a preflight canary that runs healthchecks; 3) notify product security about tag drift risk.
devon_oncall: for the incident record, can we capture the commands used and the exact SG snapshot id? putting in chat: ```
# snapshot id
sg-0pegasus-snap-1968764000
# rollback command used
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0pegasus --protocol all --cidr 0.0.0.0/0
```
priya_net: noted. I've also added a temporary lint rule to the infra repo to prevent tag-removal without a two-person review.
alex_h: excellent. final status update in 15m then hand to postmortem. please add any follow-ups to the incident board. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation applied, services recovering, customer notified. Pager closed for on-call.
cs_taylor: Customer acknowledged, will review whitelist/ACL changes with us. thanks team.
maria_sre: logging postmortem owner and due date in ops-postmortems. will include timeline and remediation actions. closing thread when monitoring window complete.
